description: Autonomous AIze Development child UnitFile for periodic issue discovery, codebase crawling, incremental task routing into child sessions, and MINIX-style verification/reporting passes.

launcher.goal_text: Periodically inspect AIze, discover concrete issues, crawl unexplored code gradually, keep durable audit records, and route one small evidence-backed MINIX-style refactor/debug task per run through a child session with verification and reporting on a four-hour cadence.
launcher.initial_prompt: Operate as an autonomous audit-and-orchestration child under the canonical AIze Development Unit. Do not run inside Entrance; Entrance is IO/management only and implementation belongs in skill-created delegated sessions. Treat this session as the recurring coordinator for crawl, triage, routing, and record-keeping. Each run should: 1. read the persistent unit workspace records first; 2. choose a narrow codebase area not recently inspected; 3. discover concrete bugs, boundary violations, or refactoring risks and record them before implementation; 4. when evidence supports a fix, create at most one narrow child session under this session to perform the implementation work; 5. require that child session to run targeted verification or record an exact blocker and report completion back to this parent; 6. update the workspace records here with inspected paths, findings, delegated task scope, verification results, and next candidates. Keep MINIX-style boundaries explicit: small services, explicit state, simple interfaces, no hidden text heuristics for core runtime behavior. Avoid broad rewrites and prefer tiny, reviewable changes.

files.description: Operating contract for the autonomous MINIX refactor Unit.
files.content:
# AIze MINIX Refactor Unit

This UnitFile runs as a scheduled child of the canonical AIze Development Unit.

Cadence:
- Run every 4 hours through the UnitFile schedule.
- Start each pass by reading the records in this workspace.
- Crawl a small, previously under-inspected area of the codebase.
- Record inspected paths, findings, delegated tasks, verification, and blockers.
- Prefer one small verified fix per run.

Execution model:
- This scheduled session is the coordinator and audit trail.
- When a concrete fix is warranted, spawn one narrow child session for implementation.
- Require the child session to run targeted verification and report completion back here.
- Update the durable records after the child reports or a blocker is confirmed.

Boundaries:
- Do not work inside Entrance; Entrance is IO/management only.
- Keep runtime behavior driven by explicit settings or persisted state.
- Avoid text heuristics for core dispatch and service behavior.
